claim: Six cell types (motor neurons, cardiomyocytes, hepatocyte progenitors, pancreatic progenitors, skeletal myocytes, and retinal pigment epithelium) were differentiated from human-chimpanzee hybrid induced pluripotent stem cells.
source: Six cell types were differentiated from human-chimpanzee hybrid induced pluripotent stem cells. These six cell types represent diverse body systems, including motor neurons for the central nervous system, retinal pigment epithelium for eye, skeletal myocytes for skeletal muscle, cardiomyocytes for the heart, hepatocyte progenitors for the liver, and pancreatic progenitors for the pancreas.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this in the text and shows it in Figure 1a.

claim: The six cell types represent diverse body systems including the central nervous system, eye, skeletal muscle, heart, liver, and pancreas.
source: These six cell types represent diverse body systems, including motor neurons for the central nervous system, retinal pigment epithelium for eye, skeletal myocytes for skeletal muscle, cardiomyocytes for the heart, hepatocyte progenitors for the liver, and pancreatic progenitors for the pancreas.
evidence: Directly stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 1a.

claim: Samples clustered predominantly by cell type in hierarchical clustering analysis.
source: As expected, the samples clustered predominantly by cell type (Figure 1b–c).
evidence: The manuscript states this observation and references Figure 1b-c showing the clustering results.

claim: Within four of the six cell type clusters, individual samples clustered by line rather than species of origin.
source: Within four of the six cell type clusters, individual samples clustered by line rather than species of origin, potentially indicating line to line variability in differentiation (Figure 1b).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation from the clustering analysis shown in Figure 1b.

claim: Human and chimpanzee species differences were clearly separated by principal component 1 or PC2 when performing PCA within cell types using allelic counts.
source: Indeed, when performing PCA within cell types using allelic counts (i.e. counting reads from the human allele and chimpanzee allele separately), human and chimpanzee species differences were clearly separated by principal component (PC) 1 or PC2 in each cell type (Figure 1d, Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this result and references the figures showing the PCA results.

claim: All cell types express canonical marker genes and do not express pluripotency markers, indicating that the differentiations were successful.
source: All cell types express canonical marker genes and do not express pluripotency markers, indicating that the differentiations were successful (Figure 1e, see Figure 1—figure supplement 3 for an extensive discussion of the differentiations; Burridge et al., 2014; Chal et al., 2016; Korytnikov and Nostro, 2016; Mallanna and Duncan, 2013; Maury et al., 2015; Sharma et al., 2019).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this conclusion based on marker gene expression data shown in the figures and supported by citations.

claim: Thousands of genes with allele-specific expression (ASE) were identified for each cell type at a false discovery rate cutoff of 0.05.
source: We identified thousands of genes showing significantly biased ASE in each cell type at a false discovery rate (FDR) cutoff of 0.05 (Figure 2b).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding and references Figure 2b showing the number of ASE genes.

claim: Many more genes had significant ASE in only a single cell type compared to genes with significant ASE in all cell types, suggesting cell-type-specific cis-regulatory divergence.
source: While a considerable number of genes had significant ASE in all cell types, many more genes only had significant ASE in a single cell type, suggesting cell-type-specific cis-regulatory divergence (Figure 2b).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation from the data shown in Figure 2b.

claim: NTRK3 is only differentially expressed in RPE and MN but is chimpanzee-biased in RPE and human-biased in MN.
source: For example, NTRK3, which plays a key role in the development of the nervous system, is only differentially expressed in RPE and MN but is chimpanzee-biased in RPE and human-biased in MN (Figure 2—figure supplement 1; Ichim et al., 2012; Naito et al., 2017).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation about NTRK3 expression patterns and references the supporting figure and citations.

claim: Cell-type-specific genes (defined as genes with detectable expression in only one cell type) were typically enriched for ASE in the one cell type where they are expressed.
source: Using a standard definition of cell-type-specific genes—those with detectable expression in only one cell type in our study—we found that cell-type-specific genes were typically enriched for ASE in the one cell type where they are expressed (Figure 2—figure supplement 2; GTEx Consortium, 2017; Jain and Tuteja, 2019).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding and references the supporting figure and citations.

claim: A broader definition of cell type-specificity (genes differentially expressed between one cell type and all others with FDR < 0.05 for each pairwise comparison) showed an even more significant ASE enrichment than the narrower definition.
source: We found that this more inclusive definition, which identified many more cell-type-specific genes, showed an even more significant ASE enrichment than the narrower definition (Figure 2d).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding and references Figure 2d showing the enrichment results.

claim: The enrichment of ASE in cell-type-specific genes is not sensitive to the choice of FDR cutoff.
source: This result is not sensitive to the choice of FDR cutoff (Figure 2—figure supplement 3) nor driven solely by a subgroup of highly expressed genes (Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this robustness check and references the supporting figures.

claim: The enrichment of ASE in cell-type-specific genes is robust to separating samples into two groups and using one to define cell-type-specific genes and the other to identify differentially expressed genes.
source: This trend is also robust to separating samples into two groups and using one to define cell-type-specific genes and the other to identify differentially expressed genes. This controls for spurious relationships that can result when the same data are used to define two different quantities which are then compared (Figure 2—figure supplement 5; Fraser, 2019).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this robustness check and references the supporting figure and citation.

claim: Differences in constraint on expression of cell-type-specific vs. ubiquitously expressed genes are not solely responsible for the observed enrichment of ASE in cell-type-specific genes.
source: Across cell types, we generally observe significant enrichments in each bin and little difference in enrichment between bins, suggesting that differences in constraint on expression of cell-type-specific vs. ubiquitously expressed genes are not solely responsible for our observations (Figure 2—figure supplement 6).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this conclusion based on the analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 6.

claim: Several signals of lineage-specific selection were detected, some of which were cell-type-specific.
source: Using our previously published modification of this test that incorporates a tissue-specific measure of constraint on gene expression, we detected several signals of lineage-specific selection, some of which were cell-type-specific (Starr et al., 2023, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding and references the citation and supplementary file.

claim: The four most significant enrichments for lineage-specific selection were specific to motor neurons and cardiomyocytes and are highly relevant to those cell types.
source: Notably, the four most significant enrichments were specific to motor neurons and cardiomyocytes and are highly relevant to those cell types (Figure 2e; Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation and references the figure and supplementary file.

claim: In cardiomyocytes, the top pathway showing evidence of lineage-specific selection was 'PPAR signaling pathway' which plays a key role in the regulation of heart morphology and lipid metabolism.
source: In cardiomyocytes, the top pathway was 'PPAR signaling pathway' which plays a key role in the regulation of heart morphology and lipid metabolism (Montaigne et al., 2021).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding and provides a citation supporting the functional role of the pathway.

claim: NR1H3 (also known as LXRA) is strongly upregulated in human cardiomyocytes as well as all other cell types.
source: For example, NR1H3 (also known as LXRA) is strongly upregulated in human cardiomyocytes as well as all other cell types (Figure 2—figure supplement 8a).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation and references the supporting figure.

claim: The upregulation of NR1H3 appears to have occurred in the human lineage based on data from non-hybrid cardiomyocytes as well as adult hearts.
source: Furthermore, this upregulation appears to have occurred in the human lineage based on data from non-hybrid cardiomyocytes as well as adult hearts (Figure 2—figure supplement 8b; Blake et al., 2020; Pavlovic et al., 2018).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this conclusion based on additional data referenced in the figure and citations.

claim: In motor neurons, multiple categories showed a strong bias toward higher chimpanzee expression including 'sodium ion transmembrane transport' and 'syntaxin binding'.
source: In motor neurons, multiple categories showed a strong bias toward higher chimpanzee expression including 'sodium ion transmembrane transport' and 'syntaxin binding'.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding.

claim: The genes in the 'sodium ion transmembrane transport' and 'syntaxin binding' categories are of fundamental importance to the function of motor neurons as sodium ion transporters control excitability and syntaxin binding proteins control the release of neurotransmitters from synaptic vesicles.
source: The genes in these categories are of fundamental importance to the function of motor neurons as sodium ion transporters control excitability and syntaxin binding proteins control the release of neurotransmitters from synaptic vesicles (Brose et al., 2019; Meisler et al., 2021).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this functional importance and provides citations.

claim: SCN1B, SCN2B, and SYT2 have chimpanzee-biased ASE in motor neurons.
source: For example, SCN1B, SCN2B, and SYT2 have chimpanzee-biased ASE in our MN data.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation.

claim: SCN1B, SCN2B, and SYT2 have been observed to have lower expression in human cortical glutamatergic neurons compared to neurons from chimpanzees and rhesus macaques.
source: In contrast, these genes have been observed to have lower expression in human cortical glutamatergic neurons compared to neurons from chimpanzees and rhesus macaques (Figure 2—figure supplement 9; Kozlenkov et al., 2020).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation from published data and provides a citation.

claim: ATAC-seq data was generated from five of the six cell types (all except RPE), with each cell type sequenced to an average depth of 184 million paired-end reads.
source: To begin to fill this gap, we generated ATAC-seq data from five of the six cell types (all except RPE), with each cell type sequenced to an average depth of 184 million paired-end reads (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this information about the ATAC-seq data generation.

claim: After extensive filtering, 73,360 peaks were retained across the five cell types with many fewer retained in SKM due to lower sequencing depth.
source: After extensive filtering, we were left with 73,360 peaks across the five cell types with many fewer retained in SKM due to lower sequencing depth (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this result of the filtering process.

claim: Cell types clustered well using PC1 and PC2 of the ATAC-seq data, except for the HP sample which clustered closely with PP samples.
source: Cell types clustered well using PC1 and PC2 of the ATAC-seq data, except for the HP sample which clustered closely with PP samples (Figure 3b, Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation from the PCA analysis.

claim: Within each cell type, species differences were clearly separated by PC1 or PC2 in the ATAC-seq data.
source: Within each cell type, species differences were clearly separated by PC1 or PC2 (Figure 3—figure supplement 6).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation from the PCA analysis.

claim: The accessibility of the promoter of CTSF was strongly chimpanzee-biased, mirroring the chimpanzee-biased ASE for this gene.
source: As an example of ASCA, the accessibility of the promoter of CTSF was strongly chimpanzee-biased, mirroring the chimpanzee-biased ASE for this gene (Figure 3c).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this example and references the figure showing the data.

claim: TSS and promoter annotations were the least divergent in their accessibility, whereas regions of heterochromatin were the most divergent.
source: The TSS and promoter annotations were the least divergent in their accessibility, whereas regions of heterochromatin were the most divergent (Figure 3d).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation from the analysis shown in Figure 3d.

claim: TSS and promoter annotations showed the strongest correlation between ASCA and ASE.
source: As expected, TSS and promoter annotations showed the strongest correlation between ASCA and ASE, and correlations were stronger when including only differentially accessible peaks (Figure 3e, Methods).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this expected result and references the figure.

claim: ASCA of regions annotated as heterochromatin, polycomb repressed, or quiescent were as strongly correlated with ASE as elements identified as enhancers or DNase hypersensitivity sites.
source: Intriguingly however, ASCA of regions annotated as heterochromatin, polycomb repressed, or quiescent were as strongly correlated with ASE as elements identified as enhancers or DNase hypersensitivity sites (Figure 3e).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this intriguing observation and references the figure.

claim: Differences in accessibility in proximal heterochromatin CREs have weak correlations with ASE compared to proximal enhancers.
source: Interestingly, differences in accessibility in proximal heterochromatin CREs have weak correlations with ASE compared to proximal enhancers (Figure 3—figure supplement 8a).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation and references the supporting figure.

claim: Differences in accessibility in distal heterochromatin CREs were roughly as strongly correlated with ASE as differences in accessibility in enhancer regions.
source: However, differences in accessibility in distal heterochromatin CREs were roughly as strongly correlated with ASE as differences in accessibility in enhancer regions (Figure 3—figure supplement 8b).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation and references the supporting figure.

claim: Cell-type-specific peaks (defined as peaks called in only one cell type) are enriched for ASCA across all cell types.
source: In agreement with the gene expression data, we observed that cell-type-specific peaks are enriched for ASCA across all cell types and this enrichment generally holds when using varying log2 fold-change or p-value cutoffs (Figure 3—figure supplements 11–12).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding and references the supporting figures.

claim: Using a broader definition of cell type-specificity for peaks (absolute log2 fold-change greater than a chosen threshold across all pairwise comparisons), strong enrichment for ASCA in cell-type-specific peaks was observed except when using the most stringent cutoffs.
source: We observe strong enrichment for ASCA in cell-type-specific peaks using this definition except when using the most stringent cutoffs due to the very low number of peaks meeting these criteria (Figure 3—figure supplements 13–14, Methods).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding and references the supporting figures.

claim: The enrichment of ASCA in cell-type-specific peaks is observed when controlling for a recently published metric for constraint on non-coding elements.
source: Notably, we observe the same enrichments when controlling for a recently published metric for constraint on non-coding elements that compares the observed vs. expected number of human polymorphisms (Chen et al., 2022a), suggesting that differences in evolutionary constraint may not be solely responsible for the observed trends (Figure 3—figure supplement 15).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this robustness check and provides a citation.

claim: The result that more cell-type-specific genes and CREs are more evolutionarily diverged is robust to stratifying by number of SNPs.
source: Although the relationship between the number of SNPs and ASE/ASCA is weak, we confirmed that cell-type-specific genes and peaks are still strongly enriched for ASE and ASCA when stratifying by number of SNPs (Figure 3—figure supplements 18–19).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this robustness check and references the supporting figures.

claim: 154 instances were identified in which a gene with cell-type-specific ASE (high dEE) had a peak with cell-type-specific ASCA in the same cell type (high dCAE).
source: Using these metrics, we identified 154 instances in which a gene with cell-type-specific ASE (i.e. high dEE) had a peak with cell-type-specific ASCA in the same cell type (i.e. high dCAE, see Supplementary file 2 for the full list).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding and references the supplementary file.

claim: Of the 154 peak-gene pairs with cell-type-specific ASE and ASCA, 95 showed ASCA and ASE in the same direction, which is more than expected by chance.
source: Of these, 95 showed ASCA and ASE in the same direction which is more than expected by chance (77 expected; p<0.005, binomial test).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding and provides the statistical test result.

claim: The promoter of FABP7 has human-biased ASCA specifically in motor neurons.
source: For example, we found that the promoter of FABP7 has human-biased ASCA specifically in motor neurons (Figure 4a–b) and that the FABP7 gene has human-biased ASE in motor neurons (Figure 4c).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding and references the figures showing the data.

claim: FABP7 is used as a marker of glial cells and neural progenitor cells (NPCs) and plays a key role in NPC proliferation and astrocyte function.
source: FABP7 is used as a marker of glial cells and neural progenitor cells (NPCs) and plays a key role in NPC proliferation and astrocyte function (Arai et al., 2005; De Rosa et al., 2012; Ebrahimi et al., 2016; Watanabe et al., 2007).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this information about FABP7 and provides citations.

claim: FABP7 shows a human-derived up-regulation in several neuronal subtypes but not glial cells based on single-nucleus RNA-seq data from humans, chimpanzees, and rhesus macaques.
source: Using previously published single-nucleus RNA-seq data from humans, chimpanzees, and rhesus macaques, we confirmed that FABP7 shows a human-derived up-regulation in several neuronal subtypes but not glial cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1; Ma et al., 2022).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding from analysis of published data and provides a citation.

claim: 'Chimpanizing' the human sequence of the FABP7 promoter at two small indels (by deleting one base at chr6: 122,779,291 and inserting three bases at chr6: 122,779,115) was sufficient to make the Sei predictions for the chimpanized human sequence closely match the predictions for the complete chimpanzee sequence.
source: While single-base substitutions differing between human and chimpanzee had only minor impacts on predicted cis-regulatory activity, 'chimpanizing' the human sequence of the FABP7 promoter at two small indels (by deleting one base at chr6: 122,779,291 and inserting three bases at chr6: 122,779,115) was sufficient to make the Sei predictions for the chimpanized human sequence closely match the predictions for the complete chimpanzee sequence (Figure 4e–g).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding from the Sei analysis and references the figures.

claim: The 1-base insertion in the human lineage at the FABP7 promoter introduces a binding site for the neuronally expressed transcription factors GLIS2/3.
source: The 1-base insertion in the human lineage introduces a binding site for the neuronally expressed transcription factors GLIS2/3, suggesting a potential molecular mechanism (Calderari et al., 2018; Castro-Mondragon et al., 2022; Ke et al., 2015).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding and provides citations.

claim: A putative enhancer six kilobases away from the TSS of GAD1 contains a human-chimpanzee sequence difference in an otherwise highly conserved genomic position.
source: Using PhyloP scores for 241 placental mammals (Sullivan et al., 2023) to assess conservation, one of the top-ranked peaks was a putative enhancer six kilobases away from the TSS of GAD1, which plays a key role in the synthesis of the neurotransmitter GABA (Feldblum et al., 1993).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding and provides citations.

claim: Part of the peak near GAD1 has been classified as a human accelerated region (HAR).
source: Notably, part of this peak has been classified as a human accelerated region (HAR; Girskis et al., 2021; Hubisz and Pollard, 2014; Pollard et al., 2006)—a short sequence that is highly conserved in mammals yet contains an unusual number of human-specific mutations.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this information and provides citations.

claim: Both the accessibility in the peak near GAD1 and GAD1 expression are only chimpanzee-biased in motor neurons.
source: Both the accessibility in the peak and GAD1 expression are only chimpanzee-biased in motor neurons (Figure 5a–c, Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation and references the figures.

claim: A single-nucleotide substitution within the HAR near GAD1 (chr2: 170,823,193) has by far the largest predicted cis-regulatory effect and most closely matches the differences in Sei predictions between the full human and chimpanzee haplotypes.
source: Applying Sei to estimate the predicted effect of every variant in this region, we found that a single-nucleotide substitution within the HAR (chr2: 170,823,193) has by far the largest predicted cis-regulatory effect and most closely matches the differences in Sei predictions between the full human and chimpanzee haplotypes (Figure 5d–g).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding from the Sei analysis and references the figures.

claim: The mutation at chr2: 170,823,193 is predicted to disrupt a binding site for several basic helix-loop-helix transcription factors that play essential roles in neuronal differentiation such as Ascl1.
source: Interestingly, this mutation is predicted to disrupt a binding site for several basic helix-loop-helix transcription factors that play essential roles in neuronal differentiation such as Ascl1 (Figure 5—figure supplement 2; Castro-Mondragon et al., 2022; Mizuguchi et al., 2006; Yang et al., 2017).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this prediction and provides citations.

claim: The expression of GAD1 from the chimpanzee allele spikes higher than that of the human allele around day 50 of hybrid cortical organoid differentiation before dropping in expression over time to match the human expression level.
source: We analyzed our previously published data from human-chimpanzee hybrid cortical organoids (Agoglia et al., 2021) and found that the expression of GAD1 from the chimpanzee allele spikes higher than that of the human allele around day 50 of hybrid cortical organoid differentiation before dropping in expression over time to match the human expression level (Figure 5—figure supplement 3b).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding from analysis of published data and provides a citation.

claim: A peak in GAD1 expression was observed in less mature chimpanzee GABAergic neurons that is absent in the corresponding part of the trajectory in human neurons.
source: Consistent with our cortical organoid results, we observed a peak in GAD1 expression in less mature chimpanzee GABAergic neurons that is absent in the corresponding part of the trajectory in human neurons (Figure 5—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation from analysis of single cell RNA-seq data.

claim: The accessibility of the putative GAD1 enhancer mirrors the expression of GAD1 in human cortical and striatal organoids with high accessibility between day 50 and day 100 before decreasing somewhat near day 150.
source: Consistent with a potential role for this enhancer in the spike in GAD1 expression during development, the accessibility of this enhancer mirrors the expression of GAD1 in human cortical and striatal organoids (Figure 5—figure supplement 5) with high accessibility between day 50 and day 100 before decreasing somewhat near day 150 (Trevino et al., 2020).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation from analysis of published data and provides a citation.

claim: Most cis-regulatory divergence is specific to one or a few cell types across the thousands of genes with ASE.
source: Across the thousands of genes with ASE, we found that most cis-regulatory divergence is specific to one or a few cell types.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this conclusion from the analysis.

claim: Divergent cis-regulation is linked to tissue-specificity, with tissue-specific genes being enriched for ASE and tissue-specific regulatory elements being enriched for ASCA.
source: Furthermore, we found that divergent cis-regulation is linked to tissue-specificity, with tissue-specific genes being enriched for ASE and tissue-specific regulatory elements being enriched for ASCA.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding.

claim: Changes in the expression of genes with more cell-type-specific expression patterns may be less deleterious than changes in more broadly expressed genes.
source: As this result was largely unchanged when stratifying by evolutionary constraint, our results suggest that changes in the expression of genes with more cell-type-specific expression patterns may be less deleterious than changes in more broadly expressed genes, supporting the idea that cell-type-specific divergence may be less pleiotropic (Wittkopp and Kalay, 2011).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this interpretation of the results and provides a citation.

claim: Evidence was found for selection on sodium ion transporters and syntaxin binding proteins that may alter the electrophysiological properties of motor neurons.
source: Most interestingly, we found evidence for selection on sodium ion transporters and syntaxin binding proteins that may alter the electrophysiological properties of motor neurons, and potentially other types of neurons as well (Brose et al., 2019; Meisler et al., 2021).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding and provides citations.

claim: Two metrics—dEE and dCAE—were developed to quantify the degree of cell-type-specific differential expression and accessibility.
source: In this work, we developed two metrics—dEE and dCAE—to quantify the degree of cell-type-specific differential expression and accessibility.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this methodological contribution.

claim: dEE and dCAE markedly improved the ability to identify matching cell-type-specific ASE and ASCA and led to the identification of 95 peak-gene pairs that had highly cell-type-specific concordant changes in accessibility and expression.
source: These metrics are largely analogous to widely used metrics that quantify tissue- or cell-type-specific expression level and applicable to any comparison of log fold-changes across conditions. They markedly improved our ability to identify matching cell-type-specific ASE and ASCA and led to the identification of 95 peak-gene pairs that had highly cell-type-specific concordant changes in accessibility and expression.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this result of using the new metrics.

claim: FABP7 plays a role in the uptake of the fatty acid Docosahexaenoic Acid (DHA), an important component of neuronal membranes.
source: FABP7 plays a role in the uptake of the fatty acid Docosahexaenoic Acid (DHA), an important component of neuronal membranes (Akbar et al., 2005; Choi et al., 2021).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this information about FABP7 function and provides citations.

claim: DHA promotes neuronal survival through phosphatidylserine accumulation.
source: DHA promotes neuronal survival through phosphatidylserine accumulation, so it is possible that the human-specific FABP7 expression increases neuronal DHA uptake leading to reduced apoptosis in human neurons during development and ultimately contributing to a larger number of neurons in humans (Akbar et al., 2005; Choi et al., 2021).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this information and provides citations.

claim: GAD1 is the rate-limiting enzyme for GABA synthesis so GABA levels are likely responsive to changes in GAD1 expression.
source: GAD1 is the rate-limiting enzyme for GABA synthesis so GABA levels are likely responsive to changes in GAD1 expression (Feldblum et al., 1993).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this information and provides a citation.

claim: The high conservation of the cis-regulatory element near GAD1 in placental mammals implies that its human-specific disruption is likely to have important neurodevelopmental effects.
source: However, the high conservation of this cis-regulatory element in placental mammals implies that its human-specific disruption is likely to have important neurodevelopmental effects.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this inference based on the conservation data.

claim: Gene expression divergence has long been postulated to be the primary driver of human evolution.
source: Although gene expression divergence has long been postulated to be the primary driver of human evolution, identifying the genes and genetic variants underlying uniquely human traits has proven to be quite challenging.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this in the abstract.

claim: Cell-type-specific cis-regulatory variants may fuel evolutionary adaptation due to the specificity of their effects.
source: Theory suggests that cell-type-specific cis-regulatory variants may fuel evolutionary adaptation due to the specificity of their effects.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this theoretical perspective in the abstract.

claim: Cell-type-specific cis-regulatory variants can precisely tune the expression of a single gene in a single cell-type, avoiding the potentially deleterious consequences of trans-acting changes and non-cell type-specific changes.
source: These variants can precisely tune the expression of a single gene in a single cell-type, avoiding the potentially deleterious consequences of trans-acting changes and non-cell type-specific changes that can impact many genes and cell types, respectively.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this theoretical advantage in the abstract.

claim: It has recently become possible to quantify human-specific cis-acting regulatory divergence by measuring allele-specific expression in human-chimpanzee hybrid cells.
source: It has recently become possible to quantify human-specific cis-acting regulatory divergence by measuring allele-specific expression in human-chimpanzee hybrid cells—the product of fusing induced pluripotent stem (iPS) cells of each species in vitro.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this recent methodological advance in the abstract.

claim: Cis-regulatory changes in human-chimpanzee hybrid cells have only been explored in a limited number of cell types prior to this study.
source: However, these cis-regulatory changes have only been explored in a limited number of cell types.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this limitation of prior work in the abstract.

claim: Cell-type-specific genes and regulatory elements evolve faster than those shared across cell types.
source: We find that cell-type-specific genes and regulatory elements evolve faster than those shared across cell types, suggesting an important role for genes with cell-type-specific expression in human evolution.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding in the abstract.

claim: Coordinated changes in the cis-regulation of dozens of genes involved in neuronal firing in motor neurons may have been driven by lineage-specific natural selection.
source: Furthermore, we identify several instances of lineage-specific natural selection that may have played key roles in specific cell types, such as coordinated changes in the cis-regulation of dozens of genes involved in neuronal firing in motor neurons.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this finding in the abstract.

claim: Integrative analysis of cis-regulatory divergence in chromatin accessibility and gene expression across cell types is a promising approach to identify the specific genes and genetic variants that make us human.
source: Overall, our results demonstrate that integrative analysis of cis-regulatory divergence in chromatin accessibility and gene expression across cell types is a promising approach to identify the specific genes and genetic variants that make us human.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this conclusion in the abstract.

claim: Humans have evolved a multitude of unique phenotypes in the past few million years.
source: In the past few million years, humans have evolved a multitude of unique phenotypes (Shave et al., 2019; Vanderhaeghen and Polleux, 2023).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this and provides citations.

claim: The human cardiovascular system has evolved to enable extended periods of physical exertion.
source: For example, our cardiovascular system has evolved to enable extended periods of physical exertion and the unique aspects of our nervous system enable human language and toolmaking (Shave et al., 2019; Vanderhaeghen and Polleux, 2023).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this and provides citations.

claim: The unique aspects of the human nervous system enable human language and toolmaking.
source: For example, our cardiovascular system has evolved to enable extended periods of physical exertion and the unique aspects of our nervous system enable human language and toolmaking (Shave et al., 2019; Vanderhaeghen and Polleux, 2023).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this and provides citations.

claim: Much of human adaptation may be caused by changes in gene expression.
source: Previous research suggests that much of human adaptation may be caused by changes in gene expression (Fraser, 2013; Kelley and Wilson, 2020; Reilly and Noonan, 2016; Romero et al., 2012).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this and provides citations.

claim: Thousands of differentially expressed genes have been identified in post-mortem samples comparing humans and chimpanzees.
source: Although thousands of differentially expressed genes have been identified in post-mortem samples, it is generally not possible to disentangle the effects of genetic differences from the effects of confounding factors such as differences in diet, environment, cell type abundances, age, post-mortem interval, etc.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this.

claim: It is generally not possible to disentangle the effects of genetic differences from confounding factors in post-mortem comparisons of gene expression between humans and chimpanzees.
source: Although thousands of differentially expressed genes have been identified in post-mortem samples, it is generally not possible to disentangle the effects of genetic differences from the effects of confounding factors such as differences in diet, environment, cell type abundances, age, post-mortem interval, etc.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this limitation.

claim: Several groups have used great ape iPS cells to study differences in gene expression in cell types present in early development.
source: To circumvent these issues, several groups have used great ape iPS cells to study differences in gene expression in cell types present in early development (Benito-Kwiecinski et al., 2021; Field et al., 2019; Kanton et al., 2019; Pavlovic et al., 2018).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this and provides citations.

claim: The use of iPS cells addresses many confounding factors present in post-mortem comparisons but introduces new issues such as interspecies differences in iPS cell differentiation kinetics, efficiency, and maturation.
source: While the use of iPS cells addresses many of the confounding factors present in post-mortem comparisons, they also introduce new issues such as interspecies differences in iPS cell differentiation kinetics, efficiency, and maturation.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this trade-off.

claim: Measurement of allele specific expression (ASE) in hybrids between two species is a powerful means of studying the evolution of gene expression.
source: One particularly powerful means of studying the evolution of gene expression is through the measurement of allele specific expression (ASE) in hybrids between two species (Combs et al., 2018; Fraser, 2011; Hu et al., 2022; Mack and Nachman, 2017; Wittkopp and Kalay, 2011).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this and provides citations.

claim: ASE has the advantage of eliminating many confounding factors inherent to interspecies comparisons.
source: This approach has the advantage of eliminating many confounding factors inherent to interspecies comparisons, including differences in cell type composition, environmental factors, developmental stage, and response to differentiation protocols.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this advantage.

claim: ASE reflects only cis-regulatory changes because the trans-acting environments of the two alleles in a hybrid are identical.
source: Because the trans-acting environments of the two alleles in a hybrid are identical, ASE has the additional benefit of reflecting only cis-regulatory changes, which are thought to be less pleiotropic and more likely to drive evolutionary adaptation than broader trans-acting changes (Agoglia et al., 2021; Gokhman et al., 2021; Prud'homme et al., 2007; Wittkopp and Kalay, 2011).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this and provides citations.

claim: Cis-regulatory changes are thought to be less pleiotropic and more likely to drive evolutionary adaptation than broader trans-acting changes.
source: Because the trans-acting environments of the two alleles in a hybrid are identical, ASE has the additional benefit of reflecting only cis-regulatory changes, which are thought to be less pleiotropic and more likely to drive evolutionary adaptation than broader trans-acting changes (Agoglia et al., 2021; Gokhman et al., 2021; Prud'homme et al., 2007; Wittkopp and Kalay, 2011).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this theoretical perspective and provides citations.

claim: The development of human-chimpanzee hybrid iPS cells via in vitro cell fusion enables measurement of ASE in a wide variety of tissues and developmental contexts.
source: However, the development of human-chimpanzee hybrid iPS cells via in vitro cell fusion enables measurement of ASE in a wide variety of tissues and developmental contexts (Agoglia et al., 2021; Gokhman et al., 2021; Song et al., 2021).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this and provides citations.

claim: There has been less focus on epigenetic differences between humans and chimpanzees compared to gene expression divergence.
source: While gene expression divergence between humans and chimpanzees is well-studied, there has been less focus on epigenetic differences, many of which are likely to underlie divergent gene expression (García-Pérez et al., 2021; Kozlenkov et al., 2020; Vermunt et al., 2016; Trizzino et al., 2017).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this and provides citations.

claim: Many epigenetic differences are likely to underlie divergent gene expression between humans and chimpanzees.
source: While gene expression divergence between humans and chimpanzees is well-studied, there has been less focus on epigenetic differences, many of which are likely to underlie divergent gene expression (García-Pérez et al., 2021; Kozlenkov et al., 2020; Vermunt et al., 2016; Trizzino et al., 2017).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this and provides citations.

claim: ATAC-seq in interspecies hybrids can be used to measure allele-specific chromatin accessibility (ASCA).
source: Analogous to ASE, one can use the assay for transposase accessible chromatin using sequencing (ATAC-seq) in interspecies hybrids to measure allele-specific chromatin accessibility (ASCA; Buenrostro et al., 2013; Corces et al., 2017; Liang et al., 2021; Zhang et al., 2020).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this and provides citations.

claim: ASCA is unaffected by many confounders inherent to between-species comparisons and only measures cis-regulatory divergence.
source: As with ASE, ASCA is unaffected by many confounders inherent to between-species comparisons and only measures cis-regulatory divergence.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this advantage of ASCA.

claim: ASCA can implicate specific regulatory elements that likely underlie gene expression differences.
source: Perhaps most importantly, ASCA can implicate specific regulatory elements that likely underlie gene expression differences.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this important application of ASCA.

claim: Two independently generated hybrid lines were differentiated for each cell type and at least two biological replicates per hybrid line per cell type were collected.
source: Two independently generated hybrid lines were differentiated for each cell type and at least two biological replicates per hybrid line per cell type were collected (see Methods).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this experimental design.

claim: Each cell type was sequenced to an average depth of 134 million paired-end reads for RNA-seq.
source: Each cell type was sequenced to an average depth of 134 million paired-end reads (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this sequencing depth information.

claim: A computational pipeline to quantify ASE was used that was adapted from the pipeline introduced by Agoglia et al., 2021.
source: We used a computational pipeline to quantify ASE adapted from the pipeline introduced by Agoglia et al., 2021.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this methodological approach and provides a citation.

claim: Two PP hybrid2 samples had a slight bias towards higher expression from the chimpanzee alleles across all chromosomes, likely due to a small fraction of contaminating chimpanzee cells.
source: We noticed that among our 25 RNA-seq samples, the two PP hybrid2 samples had a slight bias towards higher expression from the chimpanzee alleles across all chromosomes. This is likely due to a small fraction of contaminating chimpanzee cells in these samples.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation and interpretation.

claim: The correction for chimpanzee contamination in PP hybrid2 samples was conservative and log fold-change estimates were largely unaffected by contamination after this correction.
source: By simulating contamination of a hybrid sample with chimpanzee cells, we found that this correction was conservative and that the log fold-change estimates were largely unaffected by contamination after this correction (Methods, Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this validation of the correction method.

claim: A comparable number of ASE genes were detected in all cell types except SKM.
source: We detected a comparable number of ASE genes in all cell types except SKM.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation.

claim: All subsequent analyses were repeated both including and excluding SKM and obtained qualitatively similar results regardless of whether SKM was included.
source: As a result, we repeated all subsequent analyses both including and excluding SKM and obtained qualitatively similar results regardless of whether SKM was included.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this robustness check.

claim: NTRK1 differential expression is tissue-specific as it is strongly chimpanzee-biased in MN, but human-biased in CM and SKM.
source: NTRK1 differential expression is similarly tissue-specific as it is strongly chimpanzee-biased in MN, but human-biased in CM and SKM (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation and references the supporting figure.

claim: The regulatory landscape of neurotrophins and their receptors has undergone many complex cis-regulatory changes as the human and chimpanzee lineages have diverged.
source: These results indicate that the regulatory landscape of these genes has undergone many complex cis-regulatory changes as the human and chimpanzee lineages have diverged.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this interpretation of the neurotrophins data.

claim: Hybrid cells are essential in determining that the human-specific upregulation of NR1H3 in cardiomyocytes has a strong genetic component as NR1H3 expression is very responsive to diet and other environmental factors.
source: Hybrid cells are essential in determining that the human-specific upregulation of NR1H3 in cardiomyocytes has a strong genetic component as NR1H3 expression is very responsive to diet and other environmental factors (Wang and Tontonoz, 2018).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this important point about the value of hybrid cells and provides a citation.

claim: The strong bias in gene expression of sodium ion transporters and syntaxin binding proteins suggests lineage-specific selection that may have altered the electrophysiological properties of human motor neurons.
source: Overall, the strong bias in gene expression of sodium ion transporters and syntaxin binding proteins we observe suggests lineage-specific selection that may have altered the electrophysiological properties of human motor neurons.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this interpretation of the selection analysis.

claim: After extensive filtering, 76,360 peaks were retained for additional analysis in the ATAC-seq data.
source: After this filtering, we retained 76,360 peaks for additional analysis.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this number of retained peaks.

claim: Performing PCA on just the HP and PP samples clearly separates the two cell types.
source: However, performing PCA on just the HP and PP samples clearly separates the two cell types (Figure 3—figure supplement 5).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation and references the supporting figure.

claim: ChromHMM annotations do not imply that a region is constitutively in that chromatin state, but instead reflect the most common chromatin state across a large compendium of cell types.
source: It should be noted that chromHMM annotations such as heterochromatin do not imply that a region is constitutively heterochromatic, but instead reflect the most common chromatin state across a large compendium of cell types (Vu and Ernst, 2022).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this important clarification about chromHMM annotations and provides a citation.

claim: CREs that are heterochromatic in some cell types may be more prone to large changes in accessibility during evolution.
source: This result suggests that CREs that are heterochromatic in some cell types may be more prone to large changes in accessibility during evolution (Figure 3d), with significant impacts on the cis-regulation of nearby genes (Figure 3e).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this interpretation and references the supporting figures.

claim: Large changes in accessibility of distal heterochromatin CREs may be particularly important in the cis-regulatory evolution of more ubiquitously expressed genes.
source: Altogether, our analysis suggests that large changes in accessibility of distal heterochromatin CREs may be particularly important in the cis-regulatory evolution of more ubiquitously expressed genes.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this interpretation of the analysis.

claim: Down-sampling was performed to equalize power to detect peaks across cell types due to the dependence of the number of called peaks on sequencing depth.
source: Since the number of called peaks is largely dependent on sequencing depth (Figure 3—figure supplement 1, Figure 3—figure supplement 10a), we performed down-sampling to equalize power to detect peaks across cell types (Figure 3—figure supplement 10b, Methods).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this methodological approach and references the supporting figures.

claim: There is a weak positive correlation between the number of SNPs and the -log10(FDR) for ASE and a weak negative or no correlation for ASCA.
source: There is a weak positive correlation between the number of SNPs and the -log10(FDR) for ASE and a weak negative or no correlation for ASCA (Figure 3—figure supplement 16).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation and references the supporting figure.

claim: A weak relationship exists between the number of SNPs in CREs or genes and absolute log fold-change estimates.
source: Similarly, we observe a weak relationship between the number of SNPs in CREs or genes and absolute log fold-change estimates (Figure 3—figure supplement 17).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation and references the supporting figure.

claim: Tissue-specific cis-regulatory divergence in chromatin accessibility may often impact tissue-specific gene expression, although this divergence is neither necessary nor sufficient to do so.
source: These results suggest that tissue-specific cis-regulatory divergence in chromatin accessibility may often impact tissue-specific gene expression, although this divergence is neither necessary nor sufficient to do so.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this interpretation of the dEE and dCAE analysis.

claim: FABP7 is not highly expressed in adult mouse neurons.
source: As FABP7 is not highly expressed in adult mouse neurons, the functional consequences of its higher expression in human neurons are difficult to predict (Yao et al., 2021).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this information and provides a citation.

claim: Making only one of the two indel changes at the FABP7 promoter had substantial but weaker effects compared to making both changes.
source: Making only one of these changes had substantial but weaker effects in both cases, suggesting that both mutations might be functionally important (Figure 4f and g).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation from the Sei analysis and references the figures.

claim: GAD1 is lowly expressed in the cell types studied in this work.
source: As GAD1 is only highly expressed in GABAergic neurons (and was therefore lowly expressed in the cell types studied here, Figure 5—figure supplement 3a), we investigated whether this reduced expression of human GAD1 also occurs in cortical organoids which contain GABAergic neurons together with other cell types in which GAD1 is not highly expressed.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this and references the supporting figure.

claim: The expression difference in GAD1 between human and chimpanzee in hybrid cortical organoids must be the result of cis-regulatory divergence because ASE in the hybrid cells controls for any potential interspecies differences in differentiation kinetics or cell type composition.
source: Because ASE in the hybrid cells controls for any potential interspecies differences in differentiation kinetics or cell type composition, this difference must be the result of cis-regulatory divergence between humans and chimpanzees.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this important interpretation.

claim: The expression difference in GAD1 is more pronounced in comparisons of human and chimpanzee parental cortical organoids, with a higher absolute log fold-change at day 50, day 100, and day 150, only returning to equal expression at day 200.
source: This expression difference is also more pronounced in comparisons of human and chimpanzee parental cortical organoids, with a higher absolute log fold-change at day 50, day 100, and day 150, only returning to equal expression at day 200 (Figure 5—figure supplement 3c).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation and references the supporting figure.

claim: The more pronounced expression difference in GAD1 in parental organoids could be due to differences in cell type proportion between human and chimpanzee organoids or a reinforcing trans-acting effect.
source: While this could be due to differences in cell type proportion between human and chimpanzee organoids, it might also be due to a reinforcing trans-acting effect.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states these two possible explanations.

claim: A similar trend in GAD1 expression holds regardless of which GABAergic sub-trajectory is examined, suggesting this difference is not unique to a particular type of GABAergic neuron.
source: Notably, a similar trend holds regardless of which GABAergic sub-trajectory (i.e. equivalent to GABAergic neurons from the caudal, lateral, or medial ganglionic eminences) is examined suggesting this difference is not unique to a particular type of GABAergic neuron (Figure 5—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this observation and references the supporting figure.

claim: Broad changes in expression in cell type-specifically expressed genes may be an important substrate for evolution.
source: Overall, this suggests that broad changes in expression in cell type-specifically expressed genes may be an important substrate for evolution, but it remains unclear whether positive selection or lower constraint plays a larger role in driving the faster evolution of more cell type-specifically expressed genes.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this interpretation.

claim: It remains unclear whether positive selection or lower constraint plays a larger role in driving the faster evolution of more cell type-specifically expressed genes.
source: Overall, this suggests that broad changes in expression in cell type-specifically expressed genes may be an important substrate for evolution, but it remains unclear whether positive selection or lower constraint plays a larger role in driving the faster evolution of more cell type-specifically expressed genes.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this uncertainty.

claim: The complexity of the molecular machinery regulating neuronal excitability and synaptic vesicle release makes it difficult to predict the effects of gene expression changes on motor neuron excitability without electrophysiology data and perturbation experiments.
source: The complexity of the molecular machinery regulating neuronal excitability and synaptic vesicle release make it difficult to say what the effects of these gene expression changes are on the excitability of motor neurons without electrophysiology data from human and great ape neurons coupled with perturbation of candidate genes.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this limitation.

claim: Given the divergence in locomotion and motor skills between humans and chimpanzees, the changes in expression of sodium ion transporters and syntaxin binding proteins may have had some role in the evolution of motor control and learning in humans.
source: However, given the divergence in locomotion and motor skills between humans and chimpanzees, one could speculate that these changes may have had some role in the evolution of motor control and learning in humans.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this speculation.

claim: dEE and dCAE are largely analogous to widely used metrics that quantify tissue- or cell-type-specific expression level and applicable to any comparison of log fold-changes across conditions.
source: These metrics are largely analogous to widely used metrics that quantify tissue- or cell-type-specific expression level and applicable to any comparison of log fold-changes across conditions.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this about the new metrics.

claim: It is possible that the human-specific FABP7 expression increases neuronal DHA uptake leading to reduced apoptosis in human neurons during development and ultimately contributing to a larger number of neurons in humans.
source: DHA promotes neuronal survival through phosphatidylserine accumulation, so it is possible that the human-specific FABP7 expression increases neuronal DHA uptake leading to reduced apoptosis in human neurons during development and ultimately contributing to a larger number of neurons in humans (Akbar et al., 2005; Choi et al., 2021).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this speculation and provides citations.

claim: GABA release has complex context-specific effects on neurodevelopment, making it difficult to speculate as to what the phenotypic effects of reduced GABA synthesis during human neurodevelopment might be.
source: GABA release has complex context-specific effects on neurodevelopment, making it difficult to speculate as to what the phenotypic effects of reduced GABA synthesis during human neurodevelopment might be (Ben-Ari et al., 2012).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this limitation and provides a citation.

claim: Careful perturbation of the GAD1 enhancer and GAD1 expression in mouse models will be required to explore the functional effects further.
source: Careful perturbation of this enhancer and GAD1 expression in mouse models will be required to explore this further.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this future direction.

claim: Additional bulk assays such as those that measure methylation, chromatin conformation, and translation rate could lead to a better understanding of what molecular features ultimately lead to cell-type-specific changes in gene expression.
source: First, additional bulk assays such as those that measure methylation, chromatin conformation, and translation rate could lead to a better understanding of what molecular features ultimately lead to cell-type-specific changes in gene expression.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this future direction.

claim: Deep single-cell profiling of hybrid lines derived from iPSCs from multiple individuals of each species during differentiation could enable the identification of many more highly context-specific changes in gene expression and chromatin accessibility.
source: Furthermore, the use of deep single-cell profiling of hybrid lines derived from iPSCs from multiple individuals of each species during differentiation could enable the identification of many more highly context-specific changes in gene expression and chromatin accessibility such as the differences in GAD1 we highlighted here.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this future direction.

claim: Integration with data from massively parallel reporter assays and deep learning models will help link specific variants to the molecular differences identified in this study.
source: Finally, integration with data from massively parallel reporter assays and deep learning models will help us link specific variants to the molecular differences we identified in this study.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this future direction.
